rationale: The workflow already implements the primary evidence-supported optimization: dependency caching is present via `actions/setup-node@v4` with `cache: 'pnpm'`, which caches the pnpm store keyed to the lockfile (pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE; measured caching experiments show benefit, so no additional cache step is needed). The build matrix contains only a single combination (ubuntu-latest / node 24), so matrix fail-fast (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST) cannot cancel any sibling work and is inapplicable. Superseded-run cancellation (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE) is only supported by simulation estimates in the retrieved literature, and the repository's required-check contract is unverified (required_checks names empty, status not_verified); the pattern explicitly flags repository_contract_required_checks as affected and requires evaluating the contract before changing cancellation, so applying it here is not sufficiently evidence-supported. No other pattern's preconditions are clearly met with measured evidence for this workflow. Build and test coverage is preserved as-is.
